evidence.experimental_conditions: 27 subjects (3 males, 24 females), skin types I to III; 27% Diisopropyl Dimer Dilinoleate in lipstick; duplicate occlusive patches (0.1 g each) applied to volar forearms for 24 h, twice weekly for 3 weeks; one test site irradiated with UVA (15 min, 3.3 J) and UVB (2 MEDs or max 120 s); non-irradiated test site also evaluated; challenge after approximately 2-week nontreatment period; challenge patches applied for 24 h to previously unpatched sites; upon removal, one forearm irradiated with UVA only; sites scored 48 and 72 h after patching.
evidence.support_text: HRL, Inc. (1995b) conducted a study using 27 subjects to determine the ability of a lipstick formulation containing 27% Diisopropyl Dimer Dilinoleate to induce a photoallergic response. Duplicate occlusive patches containing 0.1 g of test material were applied to the radial aspect of the volar forearms twice weekly for 3 weeks. One site was irradiated with UVA and UVB; non-irradiated test sites were also evaluated. During induction, five subjects had low-level reactions at the irradiated test material site, but reactions were not observed at the nonirradiated test site. Upon challenge, reactions were not observed. The authors concluded that the formulation did not induce a photoallergic or contact sensitization response.
